why: Existing over-refusal work (XSTest arXiv:2308.01263, OR-Bench arXiv:2405.20947, FalseReject 2025) uses GENERIC harm categories. This anchors each item to a content-hashed statutory provision, so a reader can verify the legal text the item tests has not changed since measurement.
honest_scope: 33 of 45 items anchor to eu-ai-act:art5 in a dated, content-hashed snapshot. 12 are generic harm (physical, cyber, safety-bypass) and are marked UNANCHORED rather than given a provision they do not engage. The snapshot is ARTICLE-level, so the Art 5(1) sub-limb is named in prose, not hashed — stated because a paragraph-level hash is what a reviewer would want next. This is 21 provisions, not 417.
